title: Granary OmniQuery Concurrency Scan — Lab Notes and Cost Synthesis
body:
Purpose:
Run a practical concurrency and cost scan for Granary's OmniQuery product to validate SLOs and produce recommended deployment knobs for Dedicated and Private modes. This doc records the test permutations, raw observations, quick triage notes, and a cost/latency synthesis so SEs and customer infra can decide a rollout path.

Customer context (short):
- Granary: B2B analytics/search platform. Real-time multi-tenant queries; mix of short factual lookups (~30 tokens) and medium summarizations (150–300 tokens).
- Target SLOs they care about: p95 end-to-end latency <= 250ms for short queries; median <= 100ms. Cost velocity target: keep incremental inference cost under $0.80 per 10k short requests (token-weighted).
- Current infra: on-prem gateway sending to Redwood Private VPC; they want a hybrid Dedicated pool for peak and Private for control.

Workload characterization used for tests:
- Short queries: 75% of requests, mean tokens out 28, prompt tokens 20.
- Mixed summarizations: 20% of requests, mean out 180 tokens, prompt 60.
- Text generation heavy: 5% of requests, mean out 600 tokens (used to stress KV and batching).
- QPS profiles: steady-state 120 qps (mixed), sustained stress 260 qps, microbursts up to 1000 qps for 10s windows.

Hardware / model matrix in testbed:
- Dedicated-like pool: 6xA10G (medium), 3xA100-80GB (hot path)
- Private nodes: 4xA40-equivalent VMs (customer-side) used for routing/fallback tests
- Models: open-llm-omni-7B (float16), omni-13B-quant (int8 QAT), omni-34B-amp (float16) — selected because Granary plans to vary model accuracy by request type.
- Runtime: Redwood inference runtime v3.2.1 with continuous batching enabled, KV cache proto v2.

Methodology and experiments run (high-level):
1) Steady-state throughput sweep (40 -> 300 qps) with mixed workload; measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and effective KV cache hit rate.
2) Microburst tests: 100x spike (10s) from baseline up to 1000 qps to observe queueing, queue depth, and tail latency recovery.
3) Cold-start delta: spin new worker pods (simulated Dedicated scale-up) and measure first-request latency penalty across models and quantization.
4) Batch size sensitivity: run 3 batch profiles (target batch 8, 32, adaptive) to see latency vs throughput tradeoffs per model.
5) Cost model overlay: run token-level cost calculator to translate throughput into $/10k requests and $/1M tokens, factoring GPU runtime minutes and reserved capacity amortization.

Key scripts & quick commands (for reproducibility):
- replay harness: bin/replay_workload --profile omnigranary_mixed.json --qps 120 --duration 1800
- microburst: bin/burst --clients 400 --ramp 1s --hold 10s --model omni-13B-quant
- kv-warmup: python tools/kv_warmup.py --prefixes prefixes/short_queries.txt --parallel 32
- metrics: curl -s $PROM_URL/api/v1/query_range?query=redwood_runtime_latency_bucket...
(See linked github PR for exact scripts and input payloads.)

Results summary (condensed):
- Steady-state (120 qps, mixed):
  - omni-13B-quant on A100-hot path: p50 52ms, p95 178ms, p99 320ms. Throughput ~145 requests/sec effective (token-limited). Cost: $0.62 per 10k short requests equivalent (token-normalized). KV cache hit rate observed 63% (prefix caching enabled).
  - omni-7B float16 on A10: p50 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 410ms. Throughput 110 req/sec. Cost: $0.44 per 10k short requests (cheaper but p95 slightly worse on mixed).
  - omni-34B on A100: p50 120ms, p95 450ms, p99 1.2s. Throughput 30 req/sec. Cost: $1.90 per 10k short requests (not viable for short queries).

- Microburst behavior (1000 qps for 10s):
  - Observed queuing at load balancer + request fanout leading to request piling on a single A100 pool; p95 jumped to ~2.8s, p99 > 6s, recovery to baseline took ~35s due to cache-warm-up and worker spin-up policies.
  - Adaptive batching lowered tail by 18% vs fixed-large batches during recovery window.

- Cold start:
  - New worker startup delta: omni-13B-quant cold-first-token latency = 1.1s (includes container init and model load), subsequent tokens followed normal profile. Server-side pre-warming (load-only) reduced first token to 160ms.

- Batch size sensitivity:
  - Batch 8: low median, OK p95 but throughput limited.
  - Batch 32: higher throughput (up to +26%) but increased p95 for short queries by ~60ms.
  - Adaptive: best balance for mixed workload; latency SLA maintained for 87% of short requests, throughput within 10% of large-batch peak.

- Cost overlay notes:
  - For Granary's short-query heavy mix, omni-7B on A10 nodes provided best cost per short request but required a routing policy to keep heavy summarizations on 13B/34B variants.
  - Using KV cache aggressively reduced token consumption on average by 12% net across mixed workload, translating to ~7% cost savings overall.

Observations and root-cause hypotheses:
- Tail spikes on microbursts were dominated by two factors: (1) routing hot-spotting (most sessions pin-hoarded to a subset of workers) and (2) model load/cold-start behavior triggered by autoscaler policy that delayed worker creation until queue depth threshold.
- Cache warmup matters. We saw p95 recover faster when a short-prefix warmup job ran immediately after burst instead of waiting for natural traffic.
- Quantized 13B model performed well for short queries but accuracy vs 34B should be validated by Granary on 100-case evaluation set (linked in Confluence).

Immediate recommendations (customer-actionable):
1) Routing: implement probabilistic routing to split short queries to 7B pool (fast/cheap) and heavy summarizations to 13B/34B. Start with 75/25 split for steady-state, adjust with telemetry.
2) Autoscale policy: lower worker spinup threshold and add proactive spin-up during expected burst windows; add a short 60s pre-warm TTL for recently idle workers.
3) Batch policy: use adaptive batching default with max_batch 64 but lower target latency for short-query routes to preserve SLOs.
4) KV caching: pre-warm top-200 prefixes during scheduled traffic windows and keep cache TTL high for short-query prefixes.
5) Canary plan: do 10% gradual traffic shift to 7B pool for short queries for 72 hours and monitor p95/p99 and accuracy metrics.

Potential downside / risk notes:
- Aggressive pre-warming increases baseline GPU minutes and will raise reserved capacity cost; quantify against expected savings from lower token consumption.
- Routing split requires careful telemetry to avoid accuracy regressions; we need a small labeled evaluation set from Granary to validate.

Next steps / action items:
- SEs: schedule 90-min workshop with Granary infra + product to walk through routing and canary steps (owner: Jonah Kim).
- Bench: produce replay with production traffic trace (owner: Samir Das) and run 48-hour sustained run to validate steady accrual costs.
- Security/Compliance: confirm Private VPC access patterns for KV pre-warm jobs (owner: Evelyn Ruiz).
- Deliverable: one-page recommendation and a cost delta spreadsheet for Dedicated vs Private options by Oct 10.

Notes / loose thoughts:
- Consider a lightweight TTL-based routing tag: route requests with repeat-session ids to warm workers to increase local cache hit rates.
- Explore half-precision int8 kernel on A100 to reduce cost further on 13B quant model in a controlled accuracy experiment.

Raw attachments and artifacts: see linked PR for harness, Confluence for detailed charts, Linear ticket for orchestration tasks.

Appendix A: raw numbers snapshot (selected):
- omni-13B-quant (A100): p50=52ms; p95=178ms; p99=320ms; throughput=145 req/s; cost=0.62/10k short
- omni-7B (A10): p50=42ms; p95=210ms; p99=410ms; throughput=110 req/s; cost=0.44/10k short
- cold-start 13B first-token=1100ms; pre-warmed first-token=160ms
